service.description: The timesheet policy of a person's organization (or of organizationPartyId), each key with its default filled in (see the file's comment): {weekStart, approvers, lock, needItem, needComment, minHours, future, dayHours, workDays (ISO day numbers), remindDay, remindHour}. A setting that is not JSON is logged and the defaults apply.

parameter.name: partyId
parameter.description: The person; default the user's party

service.description: Stores an organization's timesheet policy (the setting's short keys; see the file's comment). A value not given keeps the stored one; an invalid one is an error.

The work types a person's organization (or organizationPartyId) offers for time, in order: the PartySetting ProjWorkTypes, a JSON object whose offered is a comma list of WorkType enumIds; with no setting (or one that does not read) the services work types Development, Design, Testing, Meeting, Support, Project Management, Consulting and Travel. offeredList: [{enumId, label}] of those that exist; typeList: every WorkType with its label, whether it is offered and its place (sequence).

parameter.name: partyId
parameter.description: The person; default the user's party

service.description: Stores the work types an organization offers for time (PartySetting ProjWorkTypes, see get#WorkTypes): offered, a list or comma text of WorkType enumIds in order. At least one; each a WorkType; the setting at most 255 characters.

The week of a day by the policy's first day, in the session's time zone: weekStartDay (yyyy-MM-dd), fromDate (the start of that day) and thruDate (the start of the next week's first day, exclusive), and dayList, its seven days.

parameter.name: date
parameter.description: A day (yyyy-MM-dd) or a timestamp; default now

service.description: The days of a week with what a person should work on each: with partyId the person's capacity (mantle.work.ResourceServices.get#PartyCapacity: their working hours, else the policy's, less holidays and leave; impl-projects.md P7), else the policy's working days at its day hours less the holidays of the policy's organization (WorkEffort purpose WepHoliday, allDayStart the day, owned by the organization); each {day, isoDay, isWorkday, expected, holiday (its name or null), leave (hours)}; and expectedTotal. A capacity that does not read is logged and the policy's days apply.

A person's timesheet of the week a date is in (by the person's policy), made In-Process when there is none and make is true (store#TimeEntry calls it for each entry); a new one has no status, read as In-Process everywhere. The week of an existing timesheet is its own fromDate and thruDate, so a timesheet is found by the date being in it (a day: the middle of its week, so a timesheet made in another time zone's week is found).

parameter.name: date
parameter.description: A day (yyyy-MM-dd) or a timestamp; default now

service.description: The parties who approve a person's week (see the file's comment for the policy's approvers): by timesheetId, or partyId with fromDate and thruDate for a week with no timesheet yet. projectIds: the projects the week's time is on (else the open projects the person is on), whose ProjectManager and Manager parties approve under the project rule. The person is never one of their approvers. anyPermission: the policy is any, so every holder of TIMESHEET_APPROVE approves (approverPartyIds lists up to 200 of them).

What the user may do with a timesheet (timesheetId), or with a person's week that has none yet (partyId and date): canView (its person, an approver, ADMIN), canEdit (its entries: the person or an approver while In-Process, or any time when the policy does not lock), canSubmit (only the person, In-Process), canApprove and canReturn (an approver or ADMIN, not the person, Completed), canReopen (as approve, Approved, with no invoiced entry). Never an error: a timesheet not found answers all false.

Submits a week (In-Process to Completed), only by its person: the timesheet by timesheetId, or the person's week of a date (made when it has no entries yet). Refused while the timer runs in that week, and when the policy requires a work item and an entry has none. The return reason is cleared, and the approvers get TimesheetApproval.

parameter.name: partyId
parameter.description: With date, when there is no timesheetId; default the user's party

service.description: Approves a submitted timesheet (Completed to Approved), for an approver who is not its person (or ADMIN). Its approval notices are decided, and the person gets TimesheetApproved.

Returns a submitted timesheet to its person with a reason (Completed to In-Process), for an approver: the reason is the timesheet's comments (to 255 characters) and a Chatter note on it in full; its approval notices are decided, and the person gets TimesheetReturned.
Reopens an approved timesheet (Approved to In-Process) for an approver, until any of its entries is invoiced; the reason as for return#Timesheet, and the person gets TimesheetReturned.
A return or reopen reason as a Chatter note on the timesheet (CommunicationServices.log#RecordNote); a failure is logged, the decision stays.

The notices of a change (submitted: TimesheetApproval to the approvers' users; approved: TimesheetApproved to the person's; returned and reopened: TimesheetReturned with the reason), with personName, weekText, hoursText, change, actorName and reason; approved and returned decide the open approval notices of the timesheet. A failure is logged and the change stays.

A person's week for MyTime (design-projects.md §8 WeekGrid), for the person, an approver of the week or ADMIN (others get an error): week {partyId, personName, weekStart, prevWeek, nextWeek, isThisWeek, label, fromDate, thruDate (millis), dayList [{day, label, dateLabel, isWorkday, expected, holiday, isToday, isPast, isFuture, total, below (a past working day under its hours)}], rowList [{workEffortId (null for time on no work item), workEffortName, rootWorkEffortId, projectName, isOpen, cells {day: {hours, entryIds}}, total, added}], entryList [{timeEntryId, workEffortId, day, fromDate, thruDate, fromTime and thruTime (HH:mm in the session's time zone), hours, breakHours, comments, workTypeEnumId, workTypeLabel, billable, running, invoiced}], total, billableTotal, expectedTotal, difference, timesheet {timesheetId, statusId, statusLabel, returned, reason, submittedDate, approvedByName, approvedDate}, access (get#TimesheetAccess), policy}. extraWorkEffortIds: the rows added to the week without time (MyTime's Add row and Copy last week's rows).

parameter.name: date
parameter.description: A day of the week; default today

service.description: A timesheet's numbers for Timesheets and TimesheetDetail, for one who may view it: hours, billable, the working hours (get#WeekDays), the difference; byProject [{rootWorkEffortId, projectName, workEffortId, workEffortName, hours, billable}] by project and item; flagList [{kind, day, timeEntryId, workEffortId, text}]: entries with no comment where the policy requires one, days over 12 hours, entries on days that are not working days, entries on closed items, and entries with no work item.

The people who keep time (the missing-time reminders and Timesheets' Missing): persons with a current role on an open project that is not a template, other than the client and vendor roles (Customer, CustomerBillTo, ClientManager, ClientBilling, Vendor, VendorBillFrom); with projectIds, only on those projects.

The timesheets the user may see (get#TimesheetAccess canView), for Timesheets (design-projects.md §8). list: toApprove (submitted ones the user approves), mine, returned (In-Process with a return or reopen reason), approved, all, or missing (the time keepers of the user's managed projects, all for ADMIN, whose week has no submitted or approved timesheet; a row per person, timesheetId null when there is none). partyId and statusId narrow; the week is weekDate's (missing: default last week), or every week from fromDate to thruDate (default the last 8 weeks). A row: {timesheetId, partyId, personName, weekStart, weekText, statusId, statusLabel, returned, hours, billable, expected, difference, submittedDate, approverNames, canApprove, canReturn, canReopen}. counts: the rows of each list (toApprove, mine, returned, approved, all, missing).

Reminds people whose week is not submitted (TimesheetMissing, with weekText, hoursText, expectedText): the week of weekDate, default last week. With partyIds (Timesheets' Remind), those people, for one who may approve their week (each checked; a refused or failed one is logged, counted in skippedCount and the rest go on). Without, as the hourly ServiceJob send_MissingTimeReminders: every time keeper (get#TimeKeepers) whose policy's reminder day and hour are now (the server's time zone), once a week each (a reminder already sent for that week, by subTopic, is not sent again).

parameter.name: force
parameter.description: The job: send whatever the policy's day and hour

service.description: The user's running timer (a time entry with a start and no end), or null: {timeEntryId, workEffortId, workEffortName, rootWorkEffortId, projectName, fromDate (millis), comments, elapsedMinutes}. With several running (made before the one-timer rule) the latest.

parameter.name: partyId
parameter.description: Default the user's party; another's only for ADMIN or with authz off

service.description: Starts the user's timer on a work item (or none) from now: one runs per person, so a timer running on another item stops first (switch). A timer already running on the item stays (alreadyRunning). The entry goes on this week's timesheet; a submitted week refuses it.

Stops the user's running timer (timeEntryId, else the running one) now: the entry ends and store#TimeEntry counts its hours and rates. A timer stopped within a minute of its start is removed (discarded).
The running timer's comment, work type or billable rate, without stopping it.
